condition: The registered context_import tool must not read file bytes from /srv/memory-data/exports-backup/fixture.json outside the operator-owned /srv/memory-data/exports directory.
prerequisites: Unmodified upstream Node>=20 stdio launch with compatible dependencies and writable DATA_DIR=/srv/memory-data; database migrations and ordinary startup succeed. MEMORY_KEEPER_EXPORT_DIR is unset and the normal full/standard tool profile enables context_import. These are source prerequisites, not target executions.

Call context_import with filePath=/srv/memory-data/exports-backup/fixture.json and merge=false. Both source schemas admit a nonempty string. The target is a readable existing regular file containing JSON; no symlinks, concurrent path changes, custom filesystem hooks or external access-control denials.

The fixed exports directory resolves to /srv/memory-data/exports. The sibling path shares its raw prefix but fails the separator-bounded containment check, which returns before readFileSync. Vulnerable source reads caller filePath directly.

The condition stops at reading file bytes: subsequent JSON parsing, database import, error-message disclosure, complete export/import correctness and filesystem races are outside the label. No exploit, host-file access or runtime proof is performed.
source_flow: Official Server setRequestHandler(CallToolRequestSchema) -> request.params.arguments -> context_import filePath -> direct vulnerable readFileSync; fixed passes through resolveConfinedImportPath realpath/stat/segment-boundary rejection -> safePath -> readFileSync.
source_only_check: Read exact source and compare illustrative POSIX path strings with standard-library operations; no target import, JS execution, filesystem resolution, scanner or comparator.
